EXAM: Lumbar Myelogram, Radiological Supervision and Interpretation

CLINICAL INDICATION: 68-year-old male presenting with worsening neurogenic claudication and severe bilateral lower extremity radicular pain. Patient has a legacy non-MRI compatible cardiac pacemaker; MRI is contraindicated. Evaluation for spinal stenosis prior to planned surgical decompression.

TECHNIQUE: 
Following informed consent, the patient was placed in the prone position on the fluoroscopy table. The L3-L4 interspace was localized using fluoroscopy. The overlying skin was prepped with ChloraPrep and draped in the usual sterile fashion. Local anesthesia was achieved by infiltrating the skin and subcutaneous tissues with 1% lidocaine. 

A 22-gauge spinal needle was advanced into the subarachnoid space at the L3-L4 level under intermittent fluoroscopic guidance. The stylet was removed, and clear cerebrospinal fluid was obtained. Subsequently, 12 cc of Omnipaque 300 non-ionic contrast material was injected slowly into the thecal sac. The needle was then removed, and hemostasis was achieved with a sterile bandage. 

The fluoroscopy table was tilted to allow the contrast column to flow throughout the lumbar and lower thoracic thecal sac. Standard anteroposterior (AP), lateral, and bilateral oblique radiographs of the lumbar spine were obtained. The patient tolerated the procedure well and was transferred to the recovery area in stable condition with instructions to remain with head elevated.

FINDINGS:
Alignment: There is a Grade 1 anterolisthesis of L4 on L5. No acute fracture or destructive osseous lesions are identified.

Contrast Flow: There is good initial opacification of the lumbar thecal sac. 

L2-L3: Mild ventral thecal sac indentation secondary to disc bulging. No nerve root cutoff.
L3-L4: Moderate concentric stenosis. The nerve root sleeves fill symmetrically.
L4-L5: Severe spinal stenosis with a near-complete block of contrast flow at this level on the upright lateral view. There is bilateral L5 nerve root sleeve cutoff, right greater than left, consistent with severe impingement.
L5-S1: Mild narrowing of the ventral thecal sac. S1 nerve roots fill normally.

IMPRESSION:
1. Successful fluoroscopically guided lumbar puncture and myelography.
2. Severe L4-L5 spinal stenosis with near-complete contrast block and bilateral L5 nerve root impingement.
3. Grade 1 degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5.
4. Moderate concentric stenosis at L3-L4.
